title: Existence of a non-normal cubic bent function
summary: Determine whether a non-normal cubic bent function exists in any even dimension at least ten.

formal_statement.body: For a Boolean function $f:\mathbb F_2^m\to\mathbb F_2$, let $\deg_r(f)=\min_{a,V:\,\dim V=r}\deg(f|_{a+V})$. Does there exist an even $m\ge 10$ and a bent function $f$ of algebraic degree exactly $3$ such that $\deg_{m/2}(f)\ge 1$? Equivalently, construct a non-normal cubic bent function, or prove that every cubic bent function in every even dimension $m\ge 10$ is normal.

scope.domain: Boolean bent functions and affine-flat normality
assumptions: Non-normality is equivalent to relative degree deg_{m/2}(f) >= 1
scope.unresolved_remainder: No cubic bent function with relative degree at least one is known in the audited literature, and no theorem proves that all cubic bent functions in the full even-dimensional range are normal.

citations.label: Gillot--Langevin--Polujan, normality of 8-bit bent functions
citations.locator: Eq. (III.1) and Section VI, item 2, pp. 4363-4364

progress.summary: The source asks for a cubic bent function whose relative degree on half-dimensional affine flats is at least one.
